jobs.title: Director of Development
jobs.description:
**About Habitat for Humanity Monterey Bay**

Habitat for Humanity Monterey Bay is a nonprofit organization whose mission is to build decent, affordable homes and provide home ownership opportunities to qualified families who live and work in Santa Cruz Counties. Habitat for Humanity Monterey Bay is an independent, locally operated and funded affiliate of Habitat for Humanity International.

**Position Summary**

The Director of Development is responsible for leading Habitat for Humanity Monterey Bay's fundraising, donor engagement, and development operations. This role secures philanthropic revenue, cultivates donor relationships, oversees fundraising campaigns, and implements strategic development initiatives that advance the organization's mission.

The position requires strong relationship-building skills, strategic thinking, and a commitment to driving sustainable revenue growth in support of Habitat for Humanity Monterey Bay's mission.

**Primary Duties & Responsibilities: Fundraising & Revenue Development**

* Plan, implement, and manage annual fundraising strategies to meet organizational revenue goals
* Supervise, coach, and mentor the Fundraising and Development Manager and foster a collaborative culture or philanthropy across staff, volunteers, and the Board, so that everyone in the organization sees a role in resource development.
* Participate in all aspects of the gift cycle from initiating contacts through stewardship.
* Meet specific annual fundraising goals and contact metrics set by the Chief Executive Officer.
* Lead donor cultivations, solicitation, and stewardship efforts, including individual giving, major donors, and monthly donor programs.
* Develop and execute online fundraising initiatives and seasonal appeals.

**Donor & Community Engagement**

* Steward donors through personalized communication, meetings, and engagement activities.
* Oversee donor recognition initiatives and maintain accurate records in the organization's donor database (Bloomerang).
* Plan and coordinate fundraising events, community fundraising, and donor appreciation events.
* Collaborate with program staff to develop compelling proposals, reports, and presentations for donors
* Support organization-wide events, outreach efforts, and public communications as needed.

**Administrative & Organizational Support**

* Oversee donor recognition initiatives and maintain accurate records in the organization's donor database (CRMs).
* Analyze donor data to tailor fundraising approaches.
* Participate in the creation of the annual development plan and metrics for corporate and foundation relations and major gifts.
* Manage the annual schedule of grant deadlines. Work in partnership with subject matter experts and Grant Writer to complete and submit grant applications.
* Support organization-wide events, outreach efforts, and public communications as needed.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

**Qualifications & Experience**

* Education and Experience: Minimum 3 years experience in nonprofit fundraising, development, donor relations, or similar role.
* Bachelor's degree in nonprofit management, communications, marketing, or related field; equivalent experience considered.
* Reliable transportation and ability to work on site weekly at office and as needed at partner locations throughout Santa Cruz and Monterey Counties.

**Required Skills**

* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to effectively engage and cultivate relationships with diverse stakeholders.
* Demonstrates high level professionalism in all written and verbal communications, appearance, and interactions.
* Demonstrated success in meeting or exceeding fundraising goals.
* Skilled in creating powerful, compelling written and oral communications for fundraising efforts through storytelling.
* Strong project management and organizational skills and attention to detail.
* Proficiency with Bloomerang/CRM, Microsoft Office, and marketing tools such as Canva.
* Ability to work independently toward big picture goals and effectively collaborate with others.

*This job description is intended to convey information essential to understanding the scope of the position and is not exhaustive. Responsibilities and duties may change as the needs of the organization evolve.*

**Physical Demands**

The Director of Development will experience frequent sitting and repetitive motion.

**Working Conditions**

Must be able to work occasional evenings and weekends. Ability to lift 30 pounds. This position requires both off-site and in-person work at a desk and at community events and partnership sites. Some occasional outdoor work may be required for this position.

**Benefits**

Habitat for Humanity Monterey Bay offers medical, dental, vision, and life insurance benefits, along with paid time off.

**How to Apply**

Submit resume and cover letter to: admin@habitatmontereybay.org. Attention: Maria Lopez.

*Habitat for Humanity Monterey Bay is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, age, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, national origin, or disability.*

Pay: $110,000.00 - $130,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Work Location: In person

jobs.title: K-5 Assistant Program Director (MUST HAVE PRIOR COMPASS DYCD EXPERIENCE)
jobs.description:
**Start Date:** Immediate

**Schedule:** Monday- Friday, 11:00 am-6:00 pm

**Organization Overview**

Veronica Arts Media, Inc. is a 501c3 nonprofit organization dedicated to empowering youth through high-quality enrichment programs that support academic success, creativity, wellness, and personal growth. Our mission is to provide students with access to engaging programs such as physical fitness, academic support, social-emotional learning, STEAM and literacy enrichment, media arts, leadership development, and early exposure to college and career pathways. To learn more about Veronica Arts Media, visit www.veronicaartsmedia.org

**Why Join Veronica Arts Media Inc.?**

This is your chance to contribute directly to an organization committed to empowering youth through high-quality enrichment, creativity, wellness, academic support, and life-changing opportunities.

**Position Overview**

Reporting to the Program Director, the Assistant Director provides site-based leadership to support positive youth development and outcomes; meet the needs of families and the school community; and further VAM's mission. A successful Assistant Director will bring a positive youth development lens to their work; ensure compliance with all licensing and funder requirements; maintain accurate program data and records; develop and implement systems to effectively manage program logistics and operations; hold themselves and others accountable for program results; provide close supervision of all activities and staff; and demonstrate a strong commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and anti-racism.The Assistant Program Director (APD) supports the Program Director in managing daily operations and ensuring safe, high-quality programming. The APD supervises staff, helps monitor compliance, and maintains effective communication with all stakeholders. In addition to supporting program operations, the APD serves as the site’s Inclusion Coordinator, ensuring that all participants—including those with disabilities and English Language Learners (ELLs)—receive appropriate accommodations and have equitable access to all program services.

**Essential Duties And Responsibilities**

**Program Operations and Compliance**

* Support the day-to-day operation of the afterschool program, ensuring services are delivered in accordance with DYCD contracts, program goals, enrollment targets, regulatory requirements, and organizational policies.
* Monitor program activities, participant supervision, staffing ratios, facility readiness, and daily site operations to ensure a safe, organized, and high-quality program environment.
* Assist with program opening and closing procedures, special events, and overall site coordination.
* Serve as the primary site leader in the absence of the Program Director, ensuring continuity of program operations, supervision, compliance, and participant safety.
* Support compliance with all applicable requirements of DYCD, DOE, DOHMH, OCFS/SACC, and other regulatory agencies.

**Program Quality and Youth Development**

* Support the implementation of engaging, age-appropriate programs that promote positive youth development and incorporate social-emotional learning, literacy and academic enrichment, STEM (science, technology, engineering, mathematics, and arts), physical activity and healthy living, leadership and life-skills development, college and career awareness, and arts, recreation, and cultural enrichment.
* Review program plans, conduct observations, and provide coaching and feedback to staff to ensure high-quality instruction and participant engagement.
* Support the Program Director in creating opportunities for participants to share their interests, influence program activities, assume leadership roles, and provide meaningful feedback on their program experience.
* Assist with continuous quality improvement efforts, including corrective action plans, monitoring follow-up, and implementation of program enhancements.

**Staff Supervision and Development**

* Provide supervision, guidance, scheduling support, and daily oversight to frontline staff, interns, and volunteers, ensuring adequate staffing coverage and compliance with required participant-to-staff ratios.
* Assist with staff recruitment, onboarding, training, professional development, and performance management using PETs and FAMS.
* Monitor staff attendance, preparedness, professional conduct, and compliance with organizational and regulatory requirements.
* Support coaching, documentation, and corrective action processes as needed.
* Ensure staff understand and adhere to safety procedures, mandated-reporting requirements, and participant supervision expectations.

**Participant Engagement, Attendance, and Family Partnerships**

* Monitor participant enrollment, attendance, participation, and retention to ensure compliance with contractual requirements and achievement of program enrollment and participation goals.
* Oversee the accurate collection, review, and timely entry of attendance and enrollment data, regularly monitoring attendance trends, absenteeism, lateness, and participation rates, and addressing discrepancies or areas of concern.
* Develop and implement strategies to improve participant engagement, attendance, and retention, including outreach to families, follow-up regarding absences or inconsistent attendance, identification of barriers to participation, and implementation of re-engagement strategies.
* Support recruitment, enrollment, orientation, and retention efforts, maintaining accurate enrollment records, participant files, and waitlists, and ensuring enrollment and rate-of-participation requirements are met.
* Establish and maintain positive relationships with participants and families by communicating program expectations, attendance requirements, participant progress, upcoming events, and available support services; responding to questions and concerns; and elevating significant issues as appropriate.

jobs.title: Executive Director of Operations
jobs.description:
About The Mead Institute

The Mead Institute exists to build mead into a durable, respected, 1,000-year industry. We do this by developing rigorous, superior standards for tasting, quality, and instruction, and by disseminating those standards through professional channels to producers, employees, consumers, retailers, distributors, and the media. We are the connective tissue between mead craft and mead commerce — setting the bar for what “quality mead” means and making sure everyone in the value chain, from meadmaker to consumer, understands and upholds it.

Position Summary

The Executive Director (ED) is the chief executive of The Mead Institute, responsible for translating the organization's long-horizon mission into an operating reality: standards that are credible, education that is trusted, and a professional network that keeps growing. The ED leads strategy, fundraising, operations, and external representation, and serves as the public face of the organization to the mead industry, media, and allied trade groups. This is a builder's role. The ED will professionalize a young field — creating structures (certifications, tasting protocols, curricula, industry partnerships) that don't yet fully exist and shepherding them toward durable, widely adopted standards.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

* Set and drive a multi-year strategic plan that advances the Institute's mission of establishing mead as a permanent, respected beverage category
* Translate the “1,000-year industry” mission into concrete annual goals, programs, and metrics
* Monitor trends in mead production, the broader beverage-alcohol industry, and adjacent trade organizations (wine, beer, cider, spirits) to keep the Institute's standards current and credible

Standards Development & Quality Programs

* Oversee the development, maintenance, and periodic revision of tasting standards, quality benchmarks, and style/category definitions for mead
* Build and manage certification or accreditation programs (e.g., judge certification, quality seals, meadmaker credentials)
* Convene panels of meadmakers, sensory experts, and industry veterans to steward standards development with technical rigor and broad buy-in
* Ensure standards are documented, defensible, and adaptable as the category matures

Education & Instruction

* Design and oversee curricula and instructional programs for meadmakers, judges, retailers, distributors, and consumers
* Develop training materials, courses, workshops, and certification pathways
* Build relationships with culinary schools, beverage programs, and trade associations to embed mead education into existing pipelines

Dissemination & Industry Relations

* Build and manage channels that carry the Institute's standards to every link in the chain: producers, retail buyers, distributors, hospitality staff, and media
* Cultivate relationships with trade press, beverage journalists, and influencers to shape accurate public narratives about mead
* Represent the Institute at industry conferences, competitions, trade shows, and public events
* Develop partnerships with distributor associations, retail trade groups, and hospitality organizations to embed mead standards into their practices

Organizational Leadership & Operations

* Serve as chief administrative officer: manage staff, contractors, and volunteer committees
* Build and manage the annual budget in partnership with the Board and Treasurer
* Ensure legal, financial, and regulatory compliance as a 501(c)(3), including filings, governance policies, and reporting
* Implement systems and infrastructure (CRM, learning management, communications tools) to scale programs efficiently

Fundraising & Revenue Development

* Lead fundraising strategy: individual donors, foundation grants, corporate sponsorships, and membership or certification fees
* Cultivate relationships with mead producers, beverage-industry companies, and allied trade organizations as funding partners
* Explore and develop earned-revenue streams (certification fees, event revenue, licensing of standards/curricula) to build long-term financial sustainability

Board Governance

* Work closely with the Board of Directors on governance, strategic direction, and policy
* Provide regular reporting on programmatic, financial, and organizational performance
* Support Board recruitment, onboarding, and committee structures

Qualifications

Required

* 7+ years of progressive leadership experience, including nonprofit management, trade association leadership, or beverage/hospitality industry leadership
* Demonstrated experience building or scaling programs, standards, or certifications from an early stage
* Strong fundraising track record (grants, donors, sponsorships, investments or earned revenue)
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills; comfortable as a public spokesperson and media representative
* Budget and operations management experience
* Ability to travel regularly for events, conferences, and partner meetings

Strongly Preferred

* Direct experience in mead, wine, beer, cider, or spirits — production, sensory evaluation, judging, retail, and/or distribution. All 5 ideal.
* Existing relationships within the beverage-alcohol trade, hospitality, or trade media
* Experience with nonprofit governance and 501(c)(3) compliance
* Familiarity with sensory science, tasting protocols, or quality certification systems
* Advanced credential in a relevant field (business, hospitality, food science, or beverage studies) or equivalent industry experience

Personal Attributes

* A long-term builder's mindset — comfortable pursuing a mission measured in decades, not quarters
* High personal credibility with both craft producers and commercial industry players
* Diplomatic, coalition-building style suited to convening stakeholders with different interests
* Entrepreneurial and resourceful, able to operate with lean staff and resources

What Success Looks Like

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
**ECSDD is a 501(c)(3) non-profit agency providing services for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities in nine northeast rural Colorado counties. The Executive Director reports to the Board of Directors and will lead over 100 employees providing residential services, day services and Supported Living Services for adults and Early intervention Services for birth up to 3 years.**

We are looking for a dynamic and visionary leader who offers**:**

* **Minimum Education:** Bachelor’s degree in human services, Social Work, Business Administration, Public Health Administration or closely related field, (Master’s degree preferred).
* **Experience:** Five to seven years of progressive senior administrative and management experience in a nonprofit, healthcare, or human services organization.
* **Financial Stewardship:** Proven capability in managing multi-million-dollar operational budgets, state program grants, funding compliance and financial reporting to a Board of Directors.
* **System-Level Collaboration:** A track record of building relationships with local and state leadership and advocacy coalitions.
* **Compliance & Quality Assurance:** Experience ensuring organizational adherence to federal and state statutory regulations.
* **Background Clearances:** Satisfactory fingerprint-based criminal history (CBI/FBI) and Adult Protective Services (CAPS) registry checks.

**For inquiries, full job description or letters of interest and resume submission, please contact:**

**Jerri Spear at (970) 522-7121 x 238; Jspear@ecsdd.org**

**Applications will be accepted until 5:00 pm, Friday, October 16, 2026**

**ECSDD is an Equal Opportunity Employer**

Pay: $87,500.00 - $105,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 403(b)
* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Flexible schedule
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Tuition reimbursement
* Vision insurance

Work Location: In person

jobs.title: Director of Philanthropy (Development)
jobs.description:
Director of Fund Development

ASAP Philadelphia (After School Activities Partnerships)  
Center City Philadelphia (near City Hall)

Salary: $75,000 – $85,000, with a salary review at six months and potential for a performance bonus  
Start Date: As soon as possible, ideally in November

**About ASAP**

For 25 years, ASAP has provided a safe, enriching learning environment for Philadelphia's young people after school through chess, debate, drama, and Scrabble. Depending on the year, we reach 3,000 to 5,000 students across the city, in partnership with the City of Philadelphia, the School District of Philadelphia, and leading corporate and healthcare institutions.

As we approach our 25th anniversary, we are launching an ambitious 10-year strategic plan to serve thousands more young people each year, and to serve them more deeply. Reaching that goal means building a fundraising effort to match. This is a year of great opportunity: we are rebuilding our fundraising from the ground up, re-engaging past supporters, cultivating new ones, and creating the diversified revenue base that will power our next 25 years. We are looking for an exceptional fundraising leader to help lead that work.

**The Opportunity**

We are looking for a dynamic, entrepreneurial fundraiser to drive the growth of ASAP. This is a frontline role: you will be in the office, out in the community, and on the phone, finding new donors, building relationships, and securing the support that fuels our programs. You will work as a true thought partner to the Executive Director and program staff, and your work will be central to strengthening our financial foundation and determining how many children we can reach in the decade ahead. As ASAP grows, so will the department you build.

**What Matters Most in This Role**

* You make the ask. You thrive on getting out there, finding new individual and corporate donors, and building genuine relationships. And when the moment comes, you make the ask, clearly and confidently, every time. You don't have to love it, but you never shy away from it.
* You lead the whole team in fundraising. You build a culture of philanthropy across ASAP and make sure everyone involved, including the Executive Director, program directors, and Board, knows their role and their next step. That includes managing the Executive Director's fundraising priorities: who to call, who to meet with, and what comes first.
* You pursue goals relentlessly. You pick up the phone, send the email, follow up, and follow up again. You set ambitious funding targets and you meet them.
* You dig in. As ASAP's lead fundraising professional, you set strategy and lead the effort, and you're comfortable handling the hands-on work that comes with a growing organization, from sending our own letters to ordering our own supplies. While we currently manage our own administrative work, we expect to add administrative support for fundraising as our team grows, and volunteers are available to help.
* You are a master of prioritization. You thrive when juggling 10 to 15 priorities at once. You know what matters most today, manage your time with discipline, and keep everything moving.
* You are a thought partner. Regular collaboration with the Executive Director and program staff is central to this job, not an interruption from it. You learn our programs deeply so you can tell our story, understand our needs, and drive our growth.
* You are hungry to grow. You want to grow the organization, grow the budget, and grow your own career along with them.
* The kids are your bottom line. You care deeply about the young people we serve, and that commitment drives everything you do.

**What You'll Do**

Fund Development Leadership

* Working alongside the Executive Director, build a comprehensive, sustainable fund development program, including systems, processes, and a multi-year revenue strategy
* Working alongside the Executive Director, set annual revenue goals, then own them, track progress, and report results to the Executive Director and Board
* Create and oversee all fundraising campaigns, from annual appeals to special campaigns
* Lead regular fundraising meetings with the Executive Director to set priorities, identify which donors to call and meet with, and prepare for each conversation
* Build a culture of philanthropy throughout ASAP, ensuring program directors, staff, and Board members understand and carry out their roles in fundraising
* Partner with the Board to strengthen its fundraising role and engagement
* Coordinate volunteers who support development activities

Individual and Corporate Fundraising

* Identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward new and existing individual donors, from annual givers to major gifts, including re-engaging lapsed supporters
* Develop corporate partnerships and sponsorships
* Represent ASAP at community events, networking opportunities, and donor meetings
* Expand earned income opportunities

Fundraising Events

* Help shape ASAP's new annual fundraising events, focusing on fundraising strategy, sponsorships, and donor engagement. We have not historically held fundraising events, so you will have a real hand in designing what they become
* Lead fundraising and donor engagement for our 25th anniversary celebration, currently in planning
* Lead the public announcement and rollout of our new 10-year strategic plan to donors, partners, and the broader community

Grants Oversight

* Oversee a portfolio of city, government, foundation, and private grants, including public contracts with detailed reporting requirements
* Work with program staff and finance to keep grant deliverables, reporting, and reimbursements on track
* Identify new funding opportunities and grow institutional support
* Outside grant-writing support is available

Donor Communications

* Oversee all donor and constituent email through Constant Contact, including the monthly newsletter and all fundraising appeals
* Ensure every message reflect
